answer: An agent network resists Sybil attacks via photoluminescent decay attestation. At the dawn of each epoch, nodes pulse a violet laser into a shielded sensor vault to excite randomized nanocrystals, measuring unique fluorescence lifetimes dictated by microscale dopant spacing. Attackers incur the verifiable cost of fabricating discrete spectrometer rigs and physical substrates per identity. However, optical photobleaching degrades emitter efficiency over time, causing false rejections.
